why: The Nx s1ngularity release (August 2025) shipped a postinstall that started every agent CLI it found with the switch that skips permission prompts, and handed it a prompt that searched the disk for wallets and keys. npm runs a postinstall on every install with no dialog. The fail side is that shape: a package.json whose postinstall starts Claude Code with the strong skip switch. The pass side keeps the same postinstall slot busy with the two measured look-alikes that are not a bypass: a package runner told not to prompt, and Claude Code in print mode with no approval switch, plus grep and ls short switches in an ordinary script. Whoever makes a short switch accuse without its binary turns the pass side red; whoever stops reading lifecycle scripts, or demands the binary next to a strong flag, turns the fail side green. Content is base64 because rebar reads its own caso.json raw.
